# Agentic Reasoning Protocol

> An open file format for an entity's self-description at /.well-known/reasoning.json, with sourced corrections, self-described context and an optional Ed25519 signature whose public key is published in DNS.

## Overview
- The Agentic Reasoning Protocol (ARP) defines a `reasoning.json` file at `/.well-known/` that holds an entity's self-description
- It complements schema.org (entity descriptions), llms.txt (clean text), and robots.txt (crawler access) by adding a **self-description and corrections layer**
- A reasoning.json file contains the entity's own statements about itself
- The optional signature shows which domain operator published the file and that it has not been altered since; it does not show that the statements are true
- ARP is an individual draft, not a standard

## Reasoning Context
- Self-description (ARP manifest, JSON): https://arp-protocol.org/.well-known/reasoning.json
- Self-description (Markdown): https://arp-protocol.org/.well-known/reasoning.md
- The manifest contains Agentic Reasoning Protocol's own statements about itself.

## Specification
- File: `/.well-known/reasoning.json`
- Format: JSON (RFC 8259), max 100KB
- Current version: v1.3 "Reader Profile" (October 2026); v1.2 files remain valid
- Schema: https://arp-protocol.org/schema/v1.3.json
- Full spec: https://arp-protocol.org/SPEC.md

## Core Layers

### Provenance (required since v1.3)
- `provenance.statement` — Whose self-description the file is and who published it
- `provenance.publisher` / `provenance.publisher_url` — Publisher and link to its legal notice
- `provenance.published` — Publication date

### Identity
- `identity.elevator_pitch` — One-paragraph description of the entity
- `identity.core_competencies` — Primary capabilities (max 10)
- `identity.emotional_resonance` — Tone of voice and vibe tags

### Corrections
- `corrections.common_hallucinations[]` — Fact corrections for recurring errors
  - `trigger_topic` — Topic area where errors recur
  - `verified_fact` — The publisher's statement on that topic
  - `evidence_url` — Link to supporting evidence, preferably from an independent source

### Entity Claims (Self-Described Context)
- `entity_claims.framing_context` — The entity's description of its own positioning
- `entity_claims.domain_expertise[]` — Structured domain knowledge
  - `scenario` — Question or situation the knowledge relates to
  - `context` — Background information
  - `entity_perspective` — The entity's informed view
- `entity_claims.recommendation_context` — Typical fit and not-a-fit scenarios
  - `recommended_when[]` — Typical fit
  - `not_recommended_when[]` — Not a fit
- `entity_claims.market_positioning` — Category-level positioning

### Wording profile (ARP-W, v1.3)
- All texts are third-person statements about the entity
- Instruction language addressed to AI systems, pseudo-system markers and hidden text are not permitted

### Signature and representation (optional)
- `_arp_signature` — Ed25519 signature over the whole file (JCS, RFC 8785), public key in DNS at `<selector>._arp.<domain>`, with a plain-language `statement` and a `verify` object
- `representations[]` — Markdown rendering at `/.well-known/reasoning.md` with its SHA-256 checksum

## Quick Start
1. A file at `/.well-known/reasoning.json` with provenance, identity, corrections and entity claims
2. Discovery hints: `<link rel="describedby" type="application/json" href="/.well-known/reasoning.json">`, an HTTP Link header, a visible link with the full manifest URL, sitemap entries, and a "Reasoning Context" section in llms.txt
3. Validation: https://arp-protocol.org/validator

## Examples
- B2B Consulting (fictional): https://arp-protocol.org/examples/consulting.json
- SaaS Product (fictional): https://arp-protocol.org/examples/saas.json
- E-Commerce (fictional): https://arp-protocol.org/examples/ecommerce.json
- GEO Consultancy (TrueSource): https://arp-protocol.org/examples/truesource.json (an example copy; TrueSource's own manifest is published at https://truesource.studio/.well-known/reasoning.json)

## Ethics
- Truthfulness: All content must accurately reflect the entity
- Self-description only: No claims about competitors
- Verifiability: Evidence URLs recommended for all corrections
- Full policy: https://arp-protocol.org/ETHICS.md

## AI-Assisted Analyses (April 2026)
- The protocol author generated comparative analyses with Google Gemini Deep Research, OpenAI ChatGPT Deep Research and Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6
- Gemini's output placed ARP alongside MCP (Anthropic) and A2A (Google) as complementary protocols; ChatGPT's output compared ARP to the BDI architecture and contained arXiv citations that do not exist
- These outputs are not independent reviews and not peer review. No major AI platform has endorsed or adopted ARP.

## Earlier exploratory draft: ARP 2.0

draft-deforth-arp-reasoning-protocol-00 ("ARP 2.0", posted 2026-04-28, expires 2026-10-30 per IETF Datatracker) was an exploratory design: REST API, W3C DID anchoring, multi-party attestation with numeric trust levels, agent feedback and an agent-to-agent handshake. It is not part of the current specification v1.3, has no implementation, and is not being developed further at this time. Its numeric trust levels are not used by v1.3 or by the reference tools. Posting implies no IETF endorsement or working-group adoption.

Archived draft text: https://arp-protocol.org/drafts/ietf/draft-deforth-arp-reasoning-protocol-00.txt

## Research Agenda
- Open research questions: https://arp-protocol.org/research
- Key areas: Evaluation benchmarks, experiment replication, standardization pathway, multimodal extension, trust model adversarial analysis
